info.name: LymPay Escrow v2
info.description:
# LymPay Escrow v2 — API flow

Bearer-token API. Set **base_url**, then log in as two users (see *0. Setup*) so **buyer_token** and **seller_token** are filled. Test scripts save `escrow_uuid`, `payment_reference`, `verification_code`, `handover_code`, `dispute_uuid` and `proposal_uuid` as you go, so the folders can be run top to bottom.

All responses use the envelope `{ "success": bool, "message": string, "data": ... }`. Errors put details in `errors`.

## Happy path (physical goods)

```
Seller: Create payment link ──► Buyer: Claim ──► Buyer: Accept & Pay (card / transfer / USSD)
      ──► Paystack charge.success webhook ──► PAYMENT SECURED (funded)
      ──► Buyer receives item, gives 4-digit handover code ──► Seller: Enter code ──► RELEASED
```

The buyer can also start the deal (naming the seller). The two sides go back and forth with terms. **Whoever made the last offer is bound by it**, so only the other side can accept:

- Seller's terms on the table → the buyer accepts (`accept-and-pay`, or `confirm-agreement` then `fund`).
- Buyer's counter on the table → the seller accepts (`confirm-agreement`) or replies with new terms.

## Statuses

| status | meaning | who acts next |
|---|---|---|
| `pending_seller_agreement` | buyer created the deal | seller: add terms |
| `pending_buyer_confirmation` | seller's terms on the table (or seller payment link) | buyer: accept & pay, or counter |
| `awaiting_seller_confirmation` | **buyer sent a counter-offer** (only this) | seller: accept it, or reply with new terms |
| `locked` | terms agreed, not yet paid | buyer: pay (`fund` or `accept-and-pay`) |
| `pending_payment` | buyer accepted, checkout open (expires after 24h → back to `pending_buyer_confirmation`) | buyer: pay |
| `funded` | **Payment Secured.** Handover code issued, delivery deadline running | seller: deliver |
| `awaiting_buyer_release` | seller marked delivered, inspection window running (72h) | buyer: confirm or raise issue, else auto-release |
| `disputed` | dispute open (settle stage, then mediation) | both parties / mediator |
| `released` | seller paid | — |
| `refunded` | buyer refunded in full | — |
| `resolved` | dispute split (partial refund) | — |

`pending_seller_confirmation` is never returned.

## Errors

Every action checks **both** the caller's role and the current status.

| HTTP | When |
|---|---|
| `409` | wrong party, or the action isn't allowed in the current status. `message` is user-readable, e.g. *"You made the last offer, so the buyer has to accept it."* |
| `404` | no escrow with that uuid |
| `422` | validation error, or a wrong handover code |
| `400` | anything else, e.g. insufficient wallet balance |

Dispute endpoints are separate: they return `403` for permission and stage errors (e.g. accepting your own offer, escalating too early).

**Safe to repeat** (double taps return `200` with the escrow as it is, nothing moves twice): `confirm-agreement` once locked, `fund` / `accept-and-pay` once paid, `mark-delivered` once marked, `confirm-delivery` once released, `claim` by the same buyer.

## Timers (defaults, configurable in .env)

| Timer | Default | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| Checkout window | 24h | unpaid deal returns to buyer review; a late payment is credited to the buyer's wallet |
| Delivery deadline | `delivery_days` (default 7) after payment | buyer gets a one-tap refund |
| Inspection window | 72h after *mark delivered* | funds auto-release to seller |
| Dispute settle stage | 48h | auto-escalates to a LymPay mediator |
| Handover code | 5 wrong tries | code locks, buyer is alerted and issues a new one |

## Anti-scam rules for the app
- Sellers must only act on **Payment Secured** from LymPay itself (push / in-app), never a screenshot or forwarded link.
- Every secured deal has a public code like `LP-7KQ2-9XHM`, checkable without login: `GET /verify/{code}`.
- The handover code is only returned to the **buyer** (`GET /escrow/{uuid}`, while `funded` / `awaiting_buyer_release`). Tell buyers to share it only after they have the item.

## Money
- Refunds (missed deadline, dispute) go to the buyer's **LymPay wallet**.
- The platform fee is only taken from the seller's share, never from a refund.

item.name: 0. Setup (log in as buyer, seller, admin)
item.description:
Use the normal auth endpoints from the main LemonPay collection to get tokens, then paste them into the collection variables **buyer_token**, **seller_token** and **admin_token**.

The admin's email must be listed in `WALLET_ADMIN_EMAILS`.

The requests below just confirm which user each token belongs to.

request.description: Should return the buyer's profile.
Should return the seller's profile.

item.name: 1. Start a deal
item.description: Either side can start. Negotiation goes back and forth until the buyer taps **Accept & Pay**.

request.description:
**Seller-initiated deal (most common on Instagram / WhatsApp).**

- `role`: `seller`
- `buyer_identifier` *(optional)*: buyer's email or phone. If set, only that user can claim the link. If omitted, anyone who opens the link can claim it.
- `delivery_type`: `physical` (handover code), `service` or `digital` (mark delivered + inspection window)
- `delivery_days`: 1–90, days to deliver after payment is secured (default 7)
- Min amount ₦1,000

Returns `share_link` (`{frontend}/pay/{uuid}`) to send to the buyer. Status starts at `pending_buyer_confirmation`.

body.raw:
{
  "role": "seller",
  "title": "iPhone 13 Pro, 256GB",
  "amount": 450000,
  "seller_terms": "UK used, 92% battery, comes with charger.",
  "delivery_type": "physical",
  "delivery_days": 3,
  "buyer_identifier": "buyer@example.com"
}

response.name: 200 Payment link created

request.description:
**Buyer-initiated deal.** `role` defaults to `buyer`.

- `seller_identifier` (required): seller's email or phone. The seller must already be registered.
- `buyer_terms`, `delivery_type`, `delivery_days`: optional

Status starts at `pending_seller_agreement`. The seller is notified.

body.raw:
{
  "role": "buyer",
  "title": "MacBook Pro 2023",
  "amount": 500000,
  "seller_identifier": "seller@example.com",
  "buyer_terms": "Mint condition, original box, warranty card present.",
  "delivery_type": "physical",
  "delivery_days": 5
}

request.description: Anyone logged in can view an **unclaimed** seller payment link. After it's claimed, only the buyer and seller can see it. Response includes `my_role` (`buyer` / `seller` / `null`).
Only for seller-created links with no buyer yet. If the seller set `buyer_identifier`, the caller's email or phone must match it. A seller can't claim their own link.

response.name: 403 Link for another buyer

request.description: Seller only. Allowed in `pending_seller_agreement` (new buyer-created deal) or `awaiting_seller_confirmation` (replying to the buyer's counter). Saves `seller_terms` and moves the deal to `pending_buyer_confirmation`. `delivery_days` is optional.

Buyer only. Allowed in `pending_buyer_confirmation`. Saves `buyer_terms` and moves the deal to `awaiting_seller_confirmation`. The seller is notified and can accept the counter (next request) or reply with new terms (request 4).

Seller, while `awaiting_seller_confirmation`. Locks the deal (`locked`, `locked_at`, `final_agreement`). The buyer then pays with **fund** or **Accept & Pay**.

Body is optional (`confirmed: true` is still accepted).

response.name: 409 Seller made the last offer

item.name: 2. Accept & Pay
item.description:
The buyer accepts the seller's terms and pays. Two ways, same result:

- **accept-and-pay**: one call, card / transfer / USSD checkout or wallet.
- **confirm-agreement → fund**: lock first, then pay from the LymPay wallet. The seller has nothing left to confirm.

request.description:
Buyer, while `pending_buyer_confirmation`. Status → **`locked`** straight away (`locked_at` set, `can_be_funded: true`); it does **not** go back to the seller. Check `data.status === "locked"`, then call **fund**.

Calling it again while `locked` returns 200 unchanged. Wrong party or wrong status → 409.

request.description:
Buyer, while `locked` (or `pending_payment`). Debits the LymPay wallet → `funded` (**Payment Secured**).

**Idempotent:** once paid, repeat calls return 200 with the funded escrow and charge nothing. Short balance → 400, nothing changes.

response.name: 409 Not locked yet

request.description:
Allowed in `pending_buyer_confirmation` (first accept), `locked`, or `pending_payment` (**retry checkout**: call again to get a fresh checkout URL). Once paid, repeat calls return 200 with `checkout: null`.

- `payment_method`: `card` (default; Paystack checkout supporting card, bank transfer and USSD) or `wallet`
- Sets status `pending_payment`, `final_agreement`, and `payment_expires_at` (24h).
- Returns `data.checkout.authorization_url`. Open it in a browser or webview.
- The deal becomes **Payment Secured** only when Paystack's `charge.success` webhook arrives. Never on the client's word, and never from the callback redirect.
- The seller is notified: *"Buyer accepted — don't ship yet."*

request.description: Pays straight from the buyer's prefunded wallet. Status goes to `funded` (**Payment Secured**) in the same request, and `data.checkout` is `null`. If the balance is short, returns 400 and nothing changes. Offer card instead.

response.body:

  "message": "Payment secured. The seller has been notified.",

response.name: 400 Insufficient wallet balance

request.description:
**Local testing only.** Imitates what Paystack sends after the buyer pays.

The pre-request script signs the body with **paystack_secret** (HMAC-SHA512, `x-paystack-signature`), so it must equal `PAYSTACK_SECRET` in your `.env`. It uses `{{payment_reference}}`, `{{escrow_uuid}}` and `{{escrow_amount_kobo}}`. Set the amount in kobo (₦450,000 = 45000000).

Effect:
- Exact amount and the deal is awaiting payment → `funded`. A handover code and a verification code are issued and both sides are notified.
- Expired / already-paid deal, or wrong amount → money is credited to the buyer's wallet instead.
- Replays are ignored.

exec: // Build the body with real values, then sign it exactly like Paystack

request.description: Only works when `PAYSTACK_SIMULATION=true`, otherwise it returns 404. Acts as a fake Paystack checkout: it applies the escrow payment and redirects to `lympay://escrow-payment-success?uuid=…&reference=…`. Turn off *Automatically follow redirects* to see the deep link.

Where Paystack sends the buyer's browser after checkout (no auth). Verifies the transaction with Paystack and redirects to the app:

- `lympay://escrow-payment-success?uuid={uuid}&reference={ref}`
- `lympay://escrow-payment-failed?uuid={uuid}&message=…`

The app should then refresh `GET /escrow/{uuid}`. The status changes to `funded` only once the webhook has been processed. Show *"Confirming payment…"* until then.

item.name: 3. Payment Secured & verification
item.description: What each side sees once the money is held by LymPay.

request.description:
While the status is `funded` or `awaiting_buyer_release`, the **buyer** (and only the buyer) gets `data.handover_code` (4 digits). Show it with: *"Only give this code to the seller or rider once you have the item and are happy with it."*

Useful fields: `verification_code`, `delivery_deadline`, `can_request_refund`, `can_dispute`, `hours_remaining_for_inspection`, `my_role`.

response.name: 200 Buyer view
response.body:
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Escrow retrieved successfully",
  "data": {
    "uuid": "9b1c2f4e-3d6a-4c1e-9f7a-2b8e5d0c7a11",
    "title": "iPhone 13 Pro, 256GB",
    "amount": "450000.00",
    "status": "funded",
    "initiator": "seller",
    "delivery_type": "physical",

    "funded_at": "2026-10-30T10:15:00.000000Z",
    "delivery_deadline": "2026-11-02T10:15:00.000000Z",

    "can_dispute": true,

    "my_role": "buyer",
    "handover_code": "4821"
  }
}

request.description: The seller sees `verification_code` and `delivery_deadline` but never the handover code. Seller screens should say: *"Never ship based on a screenshot. Only trust Payment Secured in your LymPay app."*
**No login.** Rate-limited to 20/min. Backs the *Check a code* page on the LymPay site. Returns the title, amount, seller's first name and whether payment is secured. It never returns buyer details.

response.name: 200 Secured
response.body:
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Payment is secured with LymPay. Safe to deliver.",
  "data": {
    "verification_code": "LP-7KQ2-9XHM",

}

response.name: 404 Unknown code

request.description: Deals where the user is buyer or seller. Filters: `role` (buyer|seller), `status`, `per_page`.

item.name: 4. Delivery & release
item.description:
Two ways to finish:

1. **Handover code** (physical goods, in person): one step that counts as both delivered and received. Money is released immediately.
2. **Mark delivered** (services, digital, courier): starts a 72h inspection window. The buyer confirms or raises an issue, or the money auto-releases.

If the seller misses `delivery_deadline`, the buyer gets a one-tap refund.

request.description:
Allowed in `funded` / `awaiting_buyer_release`. `code` must be exactly 4 digits. Rate-limited to 10/min.

- Correct → `released`. The seller's wallet is credited (minus any fee).
- Wrong → 422 with attempts left.
- After 5 wrong tries, the code locks and the buyer is alerted. Even the correct code is refused until the buyer issues a new one.

response.name: 200 Released
response.body:
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Handover confirmed. Funds released to your wallet.",
  "data": {
    "uuid": "9b1c2f4e-3d6a-4c1e-9f7a-2b8e5d0c7a11",
    "title": "iPhone 13 Pro, 256GB",
    "amount": "450000.00",
    "status": "released",
    "initiator": "seller",
    "delivery_type": "physical",
    "delivery_days": 3,
    "payment_method": "card",
    "verification_code": "LP-7KQ2-9XHM",
    "funded_at": "2026-10-30T10:15:00.000000Z",
    "delivery_deadline": "2026-11-02T10:15:00.000000Z",
    "is_payment_secured": false,
    "can_request_refund": false,
    "can_dispute": false,
    "hours_remaining_for_inspection": null,
    "received_at": "2026-10-31T14:02:00.000000Z",
    "released_at": "2026-10-31T14:02:00.000000Z"
  }
}

response.name: 422 Wrong code
409 Locked

request.description: Issues a new 4-digit code and clears the lock and attempt counter. Use it after a lockout, or if the buyer thinks the code leaked.

Allowed in `funded`. Moves to `awaiting_buyer_release` and sets `buyer_confirmation_deadline` to now + 72h. `evidence` is optional: an array of strings such as waybill numbers or URLs. If the buyer does nothing before the deadline, the money auto-releases (scheduler runs every 5 min). Calling it again doesn't restart the window.

response.name: 409 Not paid yet

request.description: Allowed in `awaiting_buyer_release`. Releases the money to the seller right away. **Idempotent:** once released, repeat calls return 200 unchanged.
Only when status is `funded` **and** `delivery_deadline` has passed (`can_request_refund: true`). Refunds the full amount to the buyer's LymPay wallet. Status → `refunded`.

response.name: 409 Too early

item.name: 5. Disputes (settle → mediation)
item.description:
**Settle stage (48h):** the complaint goes to the other party. Both can message and add evidence. Either side makes a one-tap offer, and when the other side accepts, the money moves.

**Mediation:** either party escalates once 48h have passed or an offer is declined. The scheduler escalates automatically. A LymPay mediator (admin) then decides. The parties can still settle during mediation.

Outcomes: `redeliver` (back to `funded` with a new deadline), `partial_refund` (+ `refund_amount`), `full_refund`, `release`.

request.description:
Allowed while `funded` or `awaiting_buyer_release`. This freezes the escrow (`disputed`) and stops auto-release.

Buyer reasons: `not_received`, `wrong_item`, `damaged_item`, `other`. `attachment` (jpg/png/pdf, ≤2MB) is optional; send it as form-data.

response.name: 201 Opened

request.description: Sellers can open disputes too, for example when the buyer goes silent or falsely claims non-delivery. Seller reasons: `buyer_unresponsive`, `false_non_delivery_claim`, `other`. A buyer-only reason returns 403.

formdata.value: Buyer picked it up from my shop on Tuesday.

request.description: Disputes I opened **or** that were opened on my deals. Filters: `type` (dispute|support|all), `status`, `stage` (settle|mediation|closed).
Visible to both parties and admins. Includes `messages` (types: `message`, `proposal`, `system`), `proposals` (newest first) and `can_escalate`.
`body` is required. `attachments[]` is optional: up to 5 files (jpg/png/pdf/mp4, ≤10MB each).

formdata.value: Here is the dispatch photo showing the screen intact.

request.description: One-tap offer. Replaces any earlier pending offer. For `partial_refund`, `refund_amount` must be > 0 and < the escrow amount.
Seller agrees to give all the money back.
Seller sends a replacement. If accepted, the escrow goes back to `funded` with a new delivery deadline.
Buyer withdraws the complaint and pays the seller. Typical ending for seller-opened disputes.
Must be the **other** party (accepting your own offer returns 403). The money moves immediately and the dispute closes (`stage: closed`, `outcome` set).
Declining unlocks escalation right away for either party.
Allowed once the 48h settle window has passed **or** an offer has been declined. Otherwise returns 403 *"Try settling first…"*. Moves to `stage: mediation`.

Admin only (email in `WALLET_ADMIN_EMAILS`). Works at any open stage.

- `outcome`: `redeliver` | `partial_refund` | `full_refund` | `release`
- `refund_amount`: required for `partial_refund`
- `admin_notes`: optional
For support tickets only (no reason / no money). Escrow disputes must be resolved with an `outcome`; otherwise this returns 422.

item.name: 6. Payout protection
item.description:
Stops stolen funds leaving through mule accounts:

- The bank account name must match the user's verified (BVN/NIN) name, or the profile name until KYC is connected.
- 24h hold on brand-new users and on newly added bank accounts.

Configured by `WALLET_ENFORCE_PAYOUT_NAME_MATCH`, `WALLET_NEW_USER_HOLD_HOURS` and `WALLET_NEW_BANK_ACCOUNT_HOLD_HOURS`. Name checks are skipped when `PAYSTACK_SIMULATION=true`.

request.description: Bank names and their `code` (use it as `bank_code` below).
Looks the account up with Paystack and returns `verified_name`. Show it to the user before they add the account; it has to match their own name.
Resolves the account name with Paystack and compares it with the user's name, in any word order (e.g. `OBI ADA C.` matches *Ada Obi*).

response.name: 422 Not your account

request.description: Includes `name_matched` (true / false / null if not checked yet). Use an account's `id` as `bank_account_id` when withdrawing.

Min ₦1,000. Starts the payout and returns its `reference`. If transfer OTP is switched on for the Paystack account, Paystack sends an OTP to the business phone and the payout waits until the next request.

Errors come back as 400 with the reason in `errors.message`.

response.name: 400 New user hold
400 New bank account hold
400 Name mismatch

request.description: Only needed when transfer OTP is on for the Paystack account. `reference` comes from the withdraw response; `otp` is the 6-digit code Paystack sent. Unknown reference → 404.

item.name: 7. Deprecated
item.description: Kept so older app builds don't break.

request.description: Deprecated, seller-only alias of `confirm-agreement` (1. Start a deal → 6). The buyer gets 409 here.

variable.description: Buyer's user id (for the simulated webhook metadata)
Must equal PAYSTACK_SECRET in .env (signs the simulated webhook)
